solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: One with inside info to leave before second drink

parts.note: to leave is to go
S is the standard abbreviation for second
a sip is a small drink

explanation.surface: An insider slips away for one more drink before spilling what they know.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Before' just places the leaving ahead of the rest; S for second is a standard abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who spreads rumours and private news about others is a talker who seems to have inside knowledge.

clue.text: Unusually powerful King restrained on losing son

indicators.note: something lost is no longer there, so a letter drops out

parts.note: sober means restrained, moderate
S is the abbreviation for son
taken as written

explanation.surface: A mighty monarch who has lost his son holds himself in check.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unusually powerful' hints at magic: this is the king of the fairies, not a human ruler, and 'restrained' is the sense of abstemious.
explanation.definitionFit: In Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream, the ruler of the fairies wields magic, so his power is out of the ordinary.

clue.text: Shock all but transfixed writer

indicators.note: all but means everything except one, so the final letter goes

parts.note: to shock someone is to shake them
transfixed means pierced through, as with a spear

explanation.surface: A writer is left shaken and rooted to the spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Transfixed' reads as frozen in shock, but here it is the literal sense, pierced, and loses its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The Elizabethan playwright and poet is the most famous English author, so a plain label for him works.

clue.text: Pressure from the past about to emerge, with views in opposition

parts.note: P is the symbol for pressure

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece goes round another

parts.note: things of the past are old
to arise is to emerge

explanation.surface: Pressure from history makes divisions surface, with opinions set against each other.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' wraps the past round the emerging, not the other way; P simply leads.
explanation.definitionFit: A divided public, split into two sharply opposed camps, is described with this adjective.

clue.text: Bound to have instant cut in relaxation

indicators.note: in places one thing inside another

parts.note: rest is relaxation

indicators.note: something cut is shortened, so its last letter is lost

parts.note: a trice is an instant

explanation.surface: Someone is obliged to have a moment of rest cut short.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bound to' reads as 'obliged to', but 'Bound' alone is the verb meaning to confine; a trice is an old word for an instant.
explanation.definitionFit: To bound something is to set limits around it, the same as confining or limiting it.

clue.text: Copy something that's still around, article filled with power

indicators.note: to be filled is to have contents put inside, so one piece holds another

parts.note: a relic is something surviving from the past
A is the indefinite article
P is the symbol for power

explanation.surface: A reproduction of a surviving object, the piece stuffed with energy.
explanation.walkthrough: RELIC plus A makes the frame; P goes in after the first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A reproduction made to look exactly like an original is a duplicate, so the noun matches.

clue.text: Frenchman goes off climbing in bad weather

indicators.note: in a down clue, climbing means reading upwards, from the bottom

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for Monsieur
food that goes off rots

explanation.surface: A Frenchman sets off up a mountain in foul conditions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Goes off' pretends to mean departs, but it is the sense of food turning bad.
explanation.definitionFit: A violent disturbance of the atmosphere with wind and rain is a clear example of poor conditions outdoors.

clue.text: Indication to stop studied when speaking

indicators.note: when speaking, only the sound counts, not the spelling

parts.note: the past tense of read, meaning studied, rhymes with bed

explanation.surface: A signal to halt, studied as you talk.
explanation.walkthrough: The past tense of read is pronounced like the colour.
explanation.definitionFit: A traffic light showing this colour tells drivers to halt, so it is the classic signal.

clue.text: Urge to restrict first couple of ringing bells

indicators.note: to restrict is to hem in, so one piece encloses another

parts.note: to call on someone is to urge them

indicators.note: the first couple means the opening two letters are kept

parts.note: the opening pair of letters

explanation.surface: A plea to limit the first peals of the bells.
explanation.walkthrough: CALL ON takes RI after its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A set of tuned bells in a tower, played from a keyboard, is known by this name.

clue.text: Measure of processing speed for plate needing development

indicators.note: something needing development must be worked into a new form

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A photographic plate awaiting development, with a speed rating attached.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Development' suggests photography, but it tells you to rework the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A computer's speed is rated in floating-point operations per second, and a trillion of them is this unit.

clue.text: Bishop ignoring limits in requirements for clergy?

indicators.note: to ignore something is to leave it out

parts.note: borders are limits or boundaries
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A bishop disregarding the rules for his clergy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ignoring limits' tempts you to drop the outside letters of 'Bishop'; instead B is dropped from BORDERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Priests must take holy orders to be ordained, and orders are also commands or requirements, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Regrets first couple of options returned person of no substance

indicators.note: something returned goes back the way it came

parts.note: to rue is to regret

indicators.note: the first couple means the opening two letters are kept

parts.note: the opening pair of letters

explanation.surface: Someone shallow regrets that the first choices came back.
explanation.walkthrough: RUES then OP, all read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A pretentious person puts on airs to impress, so behind the act there is little real depth.

clue.text: Still recalled Michigan, going to city in Alabama

indicators.note: something recalled is called back, so it runs the other way

parts.note: MI is the postal abbreviation for Michigan
Mobile is a port city in Alabama

explanation.surface: Someone still remembers Michigan while heading to Alabama.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Still' reads as 'even now'; it is the adjective meaning motionless.
explanation.definitionFit: Something motionless, not moving at all, is still in the physical sense.

clue.text: Corporation shaken with steps this person takes?

definitions.text: Corporation shaken with steps this person takes?

parts.words: Corporation shaken with steps this person takes?
parts.note: surface: a company rocked by measures its boss introduces

parts.words: Corporation shaken with steps this person takes?
parts.note: setter's reading: a performer whose paunch wobbles as she moves her feet

explanation.walkthrough: Corporation is an old joke word for a pot belly, and steps are dance steps, not business measures.
explanation.definitionFit: A performer of the Middle Eastern dance shakes the midriff while stepping, which is exactly the picture drawn.

clue.text: Collection of letters in which X frequently appears?

definitions.text: Collection of letters in which X frequently appears?

parts.words: Collection of letters in which X frequently appears?
parts.note: surface: an alphabet or word game where one letter keeps turning up

parts.words: Collection of letters in which X frequently appears?
parts.note: setter's reading: mailed voting papers, each marked with a cross

explanation.walkthrough: Letters means mail, not the alphabet, and X is the cross a voter marks on a paper.
explanation.definitionFit: A vote gathered by mail collects many envelopes, each containing a paper marked with a cross.

clue.text: American guy lying to shake off other guys? Awesome!

parts.note: bo is US slang for a pal or fellow

indicators.note: to shake something off is to get rid of it

parts.note: mendacious means lying
men are guys

explanation.surface: An American fellow lying to escape his mates, to a cry of admiration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Other guys' refers back to the first guy: MEN leaves MENDACIOUS.
explanation.definitionFit: It is American slang for excellent or impressive, an exclamation of admiration like the definition.

clue.text: Exhausted and heading away from dance, considering everything

indicators.note: the heading is the front, so the first letter departs

parts.note: all in means exhausted
a ball is a formal dance

explanation.surface: Worn out and leaving the dance, when you think about it.
explanation.walkthrough: ALL IN is British informal for worn out; BALL loses its B.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase sums things up, taking every factor into account, the same as the definition.

clue.text: A large country, good weather, without rain — everyone will appear

parts.note: taken as written
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large
a land is a country
sunshine is good weather
dry weather has no rain

explanation.surface: A big sunny country with no rain will draw a crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: The five pieces run in clue order.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means every single person, without exception, so it matches the pronoun.

clue.text: Brave to yield leadership to multinational force — and doomed

indicators.note: yielding the lead means the first letter hands its place over

parts.note: plucky means brave
UN peacekeepers are a multinational force

explanation.surface: A brave soldier cedes command to an international force and is done for.
explanation.walkthrough: The P that leads PLUCKY is replaced by UN.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone ill-fated, with fortune set against them, can be described as having no luck.

clue.text: Repository finding value in silence

indicators.note: in places one thing inside another

parts.note: mum means silent, as in 'keep mum'
use is value, as in 'of no use'

explanation.surface: A storehouse where worth is found in quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: Mum for silence comes from the idiom 'keep mum', meaning say nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A building where historical or artistic objects are stored and displayed is a place of keeping, a store.

clue.text: Defeat inspiring passion with defensive system

indicators.note: to inspire is literally to breathe in, so one piece takes others inside

parts.note: a fall is a defeat
ire is anger, a strong passion
W is the abbreviation for with

explanation.surface: A defeat that stirs passion in those with a strong defence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inspiring' looks like praise but means breathing in; W for with is a standard abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Computer networks are protected by software or hardware that blocks unauthorised traffic, a security barrier.

clue.text: Tree from area almost used up

indicators.note: almost means not quite complete, so the last letter goes

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for area
spent means used up

explanation.surface: Timber from a region that is nearly exhausted.
explanation.walkthrough: SPENT drops its T after A.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a poplar with trembling leaves, a species of woodland plant.

clue.text: Support group? Most of family quite failing to get it

indicators.note: most of something is all but a bit, so the last letter goes
failing to get something means going without it, so letters are removed

parts.note: a clan is an extended family
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A family that does not quite get it looks for a support group.
explanation.walkthrough: CLAN loses N; QUITE loses IT. A group hired to applaud gives 'support' a twist, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A body of people paid to clap at a performance is a set of hired backers in the theatre.

clue.text: Humming sound almost entirely backing beat

indicators.note: backing means going backwards
almost means not quite complete, so the last letter goes

parts.note: a purr is a low humming sound
all means entirely, wholly

explanation.surface: A humming noise almost entirely supports the rhythm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backing beat' sounds like a musical accompaniment; 'beat' is the verb to thrash.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a dialect or informal verb for thrashing or hitting someone hard.

clue.text: Odd slice removed from cut of beef?

indicators.note: a slice taken off the end shortens what remains by one letter

parts.note: rump is a cut of beef from the hindquarters

explanation.surface: A strange piece cut off from a joint of beef.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang rum means strange, as in 'a rum business'.
explanation.definitionFit: The informal British adjective means peculiar or strange, so it replaces the definition directly.

clue.text: Some Balkan swindler always ignoring a note

indicators.note: ignoring every time means removing each occurrence, not just one

parts.note: a Croat is one kind of Balkan person
a cheat is a swindler
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Balkan conman who never pays attention to a message.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Always' means both A's go, from CROAT and from CHEAT.
explanation.definitionFit: In music this is a symbol worth one beat, a quarter note in American terms.

clue.text: Male bikers, as it were, cycling — pardon?

indicators.note: going round in a cycle moves letters from the front to the back

parts.note: bikers cycle; 'as it were' flags the loose reading
men are males

explanation.surface: Male bikers out riding ask for forgiveness.
explanation.walkthrough: CYCLE MEN makes cyclists; move the opening CY to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Mercy shown to an offender, especially forgiveness from a ruler or court, is the noun sense of pardon.

clue.text: Quiet tear about Mike reveals weak character

parts.note: sh is a call for quiet

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece goes round another

parts.note: a rip is a tear
Mike is M in the radio alphabet

explanation.surface: A silent tear over Mike shows he is a feeble type.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tear' wants to be a teardrop, rhyming with fear; it is the rip, rhyming with fair.
explanation.definitionFit: A small, puny or feeble person is informally called by the name of the tiny crustacean.
